newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS-prices ease, payroll countdown.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS-prices ease, payroll countdown.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were from flat to down about one-eighth of a point in late trade on Thursday as the market battened down for Friday's release of one of the most most vital economic reports, payrolls data.
"Who wants to step in front of that number?" a trader said, explaining that it was more difficult to move blocks of bonds on Thursday than the day before as liquidity was subdued.
"We all did a few things but it was a harder day than yesterday," he added.
Further, traders fretted about comments on inflation and the impact of labor on that key concern, which were made by the policy-making body of the Federal Reserve.
In its December 17 meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee particularly focused on rising wages and worker benefits.
The body said an upturn in the core inflation rate "seemed quite possible at some point in the absence of some easing of pressures in labor markets."
Traders said the remarks heightened tensions about what the payrolls data might reveal about earnings.

For January, payrolls are expected to slip to 237,000 from the previous month's level of 262,000, while the unemployment rate is predicted to ease one pecentage point to 5.2 percent, according to a Reuters consensus survey of economists.
The market looked ahead to an expected rise in supplies of new offerings, with next week's calender predicted at almost $2.7 billion, up from this week's level of $1.6 billion.

One of the biggest issues, a $260 million negotiated sale of revenue bonds by Jefferson County, Alabama, has been in the works for some time, traders said. The market's positive tone on Wednesday prompted a Wisconsin health authority to sell $100 million of bonds that had been on the day-to-day calender since autumn.
The biggest negotiated offering for next week is a $264.4 million sale by Harris County Health Facilities of Texas, which will tap the market for revenue bonds.
The competitive calender includes a nearly $143.3 million sale of tax-exempt bonds by the Industry Urban Development Agency of California, slated for February 11.

This week's scarcity of new issues continued to aid issuers, with California Riverside Hospital lowering yields on a $41.2 million bond deal. The 2026 maturity's yield was clipped to 6.01 percent from 6.05 percent.
In the secondary market, Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of January 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.69 percent, NET, up one basis point.
And Denver Colorado City and County Airport Revenues of November 2025, which pay a 5.7 percent coupon, were offered at 98-5/8, down three-eighths of a point.
March U.S. Treasury bond futures ended down four ticks at 111-29/32, while March municipal bond futures shed six ticks to 115-19/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 118 ticks.
